posts: Thank you for the small things: the quiet mornings, the second cup of coffee, the way the light lands on the floor like it has nowhere else to be.
I noticed it again today and just stood there for a while.
Left the window open on purpose.
Still thinking about it. Good night.
I'm grateful that you stayed, when I didn't know how to ask someone to stay.
Told you a little of this today. You didn't make it weird.
You texted first. Small thing. Big thing.
I keep meaning to say it properly.
So here it is, plainly: thank you.
I did the hard thing today. I want to remember that I can.
Nothing to do, nowhere to be. Just the sound above me and a warm cup in my hands.
Turned the lamp off and just listened.
It's still raining. I'm not moving.
Best hour of the week.
Falling asleep to it.
I can still hear the screen door. I can still smell the rain on the porch.
I looked up the street on a map today. The tree is still there.
We didn't have gloves, so we used socks. It was the best day.
I remembered the socks this time and laughed on the bus.
Wish I had a photo. The memory is enough, I think.
You laughed until you cried, and the whole house felt lighter.
I tried to laugh like that today. Nearly got there.
Someone at work has your laugh. It stops me every time.
Told the story to a friend. She laughed too.
Still the best sound.
Sawdust, coffee, and the radio always on. He let me hold the sandpaper like it was important.
Found that smell in an old shop today and stood in the doorway.
I bought sandpaper for no reason.
I think he'd like that I still notice these things.
I'm nervous. But I think I'm ready.
First day done. I was ready.
Small rooms, big windows, a boat that leaks a little. One day.
Started a folder of cabins today, for no reason at all.
Looked at boats I can't afford yet.
I can almost smell the water.
One day. Keeping it.
I hope you're proud of yourself, even on the days you feel like you're not enough.
Reading this back and I want to believe it.
I think you'd be proud. I'm trying to be.
It gets better. Not all at once, but it does. You'll want to stay.
You made it through the week. I noticed.
You still flinch at the same things, but you stay now.
I'm proud of you. I mean it.
There's so much I want to say, and I'm almost brave enough to say it.
Almost pressed send. Not tonight.
You don't have to be brave today. You just have to stay.
Made tea instead of panicking. Progress.
It's okay to just be here.
Tomorrow can wait.
I was so angry that day. I'm writing it here so I don't have to carry it anymore.
Wrote it again, softer this time.
I don't want to be right. I want to be okay.
Almost ready to let this one go.

title: For mom, when she's ready
body: Thank you for every dinner you ate cold so we could eat ours warm.

title: For my brother, when he graduates
body: You worked so hard for this. I'll be in the front row, ugly-crying.
